title: Fiskesuppa
subtitle: scandinavian creamy fish soup
excerpt: Fiskesuppa is a light, creamy Scandinavian fish soup made with cod, salmon and root vegetables in a dill-scented broth. It comes together in under 30 minutes. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Fish soups of this style are eaten across coastal Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Each region has its own variation, but cream, root vegetables and fresh herbs are constants.

glossaryTerms.definition: Scandinavian fish soup, typically creamy with root vegetables and fresh herbs.
Cooking food gently in barely simmering liquid.

content.text: is a gentle, satisfying soup that lets the fish speak clearly. The base is a simple broth of stock, carrot, potato and leek, enriched with cream at the end. The fish goes in last and is
very briefly so it stays tender and does not overcook.
Using two fish gives the soup more depth: cod gives a clean, flaky texture while salmon adds richness and colour. Fresh dill stirred in at the end keeps the flavour bright.
Melt the butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Add the leek and carrot and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the potato and pour in the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 12 minutes until the potato is just tender.
Pour in the cream and stir to combine. Season to taste and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the cod and salmon chunks. Poach gently for 4 to 5 minutes until the fish just flakes when pressed. Do not stir vigorously or the fish will break apart.
Remove from the heat and stir in the fresh dill. Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

attrs.problem: The fish is rubbery and overcooked.
attrs.solution: The soup was too hot or the fish was left in too long. Keep the soup at a gentle simmer, not a boil, and check the fish after 4 minutes.

attrs.problem: The cream has curdled in the soup.
attrs.solution: The heat was too high after adding the cream. Always add cream to a soup that is simmering gently, not boiling hard.
Use a good quality fish or chicken stock. Season well at the end and add more dill. A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the whole dish.

content.text: Fiskesuppa is everyday cooking in coastal Scandinavian towns. Fishing communities along the Norwegian fjords have made versions of this soup for generations. It is a weeknight meal, eaten with bread and butter. Every household has its own variation based on what the boats brought in.
